Want to live in Europe without buying property?

There’s a visa most Indians have never heard of.

I asked immigration expert Deepesh Deshmukh about the easiest way to move to Europe.

His answer?

Greece's Financially Independent Person (FIP) Visa.

If you can show around €3,500/month in passive income or roughly ₹45 lakh in savings, you can apply for a 3-year visa.

The best part?

You can continue working remotely for your Indian employer while living in Greece.

The only question is...

Would you move to Greece if you could keep your Indian salary?

$1.2 billion in debt.

Most people would panic.

Robert Kiyosaki smiled.

The Rich Dad Poor Dad author says he uses debt differently: not to buy liabilities, but to acquire assets that generate cash flow.

Instead of selling properties and paying tax, he refinances them, unlocks the equity, and uses that money to buy more.

That’s how leverage can become a wealth-building machine.

But here’s the part people skip: this strategy works only if the assets keep performing. When markets crash, debt compounds too.

As Kiyosaki puts it: Don’t copy me. This is a strategy for pros.

Amitabh Bachchan went from ₹90 Cr in debt to rebuilding his career; and the lesson isn’t about movies.

In the 1990s, he tried to build an empire through ABCL. It collapsed, leaving him with massive debt, legal cases and creditors at his doorstep.

Then came KBC.

The biggest lesson? Sometimes, the smartest financial move isn’t chasing something new. It’s recognising the asset you already have and finding a way to turn it into cash flow.

Know what you’re worth. Build around it.
